findings.consequence: A pallet jam at the conveyor entry photo-eye will never be detected. Motor Y10 will continue to drive against the jammed pallet, creating risk of battery pack damage, mechanical failure, conveyor motor overheating, and failure to annunciate the jam alarm to line operators.
findings.evidence: Cause-and-effect matrix CE-ST10-03 requires that if conveyor entry photo-eye PE-1002 (X11) is blocked for more than 5.0 s while the conveyor is running, the conveyor motor stops and a jam alarm is raised. The parameter sheet specifies jam_time as 5.0 s on timer T10. The lint report identifies X11 as defined in the I/O list but never used. In the program, R2 resets M190 and R3 includes M190 in the common stop relay M199, but the logic to time the jam (starting T10 when Y10 and X11 are active) and latch M190 upon T10 done is completely missing.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the missing jam detection rungs: drive timer T10 when conveyor is running (Y10) and entry photo-eye is blocked (X11), and latch jam alarm M190 upon T10 done: LD Y10; AND X11; OUT T10 K50; LD T10; SET M190.
findings.title: Missing conveyor jam detection logic and timer T10

findings.consequence: Conveyor motor Y10 will automatically restart without operator intervention or pressing Fault Reset pushbutton PB-0002 (X1) as soon as the overload cools down, violating machinery safety standards (IEC 60204-1 / NFPA 79) and endangering maintenance personnel.
findings.evidence: In R1, LDI X13 drives M191 with an unlatched OUT coil. In R3, M191 energizes stop relay M199, which turns off conveyor motor contactor Y10 in R4. Reset rung R2 only resets M190, omitting M191. Narrative section 4.8 states that latched alarms clear with fault reset once their cause has gone. If an overload occurs, X13 opens (trips) and stops the conveyor. When the motor overload relay cools down or auto-resets, X13 returns to 24 V (healthy), immediately de-energizing M191 and clearing M199.
findings.proposed_fix: Latch the overload alarm with SET M191 in R1, and add RST M191 to reset rung R2 conditioned on PB-0002 (X1): In R1: LDI X13; SET M191. In R2: LD X1; RST M190; RST M191.
findings.title: Conveyor motor overload alarm M191 is unlatched causing unexpected automatic restart

findings.consequence: Resetting the hardwired E-stop safety circuit directly restarts hazardous motion on conveyor motor Y10 without requiring a fault reset or intentional restart action, violating ISO 13850 section 4.1.4 and IEC 60204-1 section 9.2.5.4.2.
findings.evidence: In R3, ORI X0 is wired directly into stop relay M199. When E-stop healthy input X0 drops to 0, M199 turns ON, de-energizing Y10 in R4. When the E-stop safety relay is reset and X0 returns to 1, ORI X0 immediately clears M199 to 0. Since Auto mode selector SS-0003 (X2) is a maintained switch that remains ON, Y10 immediately re-energizes.
findings.proposed_fix: Require a manual fault reset (PB-0002 / X1) to clear the fault state following an E-stop event by latching an E-stop tripped fault condition that must be acknowledged and reset before M199 can clear and allow Y10 to re-energize.
findings.title: Conveyor motor Y10 automatically restarts upon E-stop circuit reset without manual intervention

findings.consequence: If RQ-1005 is pulsed while the conveyor is stopped, faulted, in manual mode, or during an active E-stop, stopper solenoid Y11 will energize and drop the stopper. If no pallet is present, an approaching pallet can bypass the test station untested. If the conveyor is not running, the pallet will not leave during the 2.0 s pulse and the stopper will extend again, risking mechanical jam or equipment damage.
findings.evidence: Rung R6 fires solely on the rising edge of RQ-1005 (LDP X14) to SET Y11 without verifying Auto mode (X2), E-stop healthy (X0), ST10 fault status (ANI M199), conveyor running (Y10), or pallet presence at the stop (PE-1001 / X10 / M100).
findings.proposed_fix: Add interlocks to R6 so Y11 can only be set when the cell is in Auto mode (X2), E-stop is healthy (X0), no ST10 fault is active (ANI M199), the conveyor is running (Y10), and a pallet is confirmed present at the stop (M100): LD X2; AND X0; ANI M199; AND Y10; AND M100; ANDP X14; SET Y11.
findings.title: Stopper release solenoid Y11 lacks operational interlocks and safety checks

data.summary: The ST10 conveyor program contains critical logic and safety deficiencies. The conveyor jam detection logic required by CE-ST10-03 and narrative section 3 is completely missing (PE-1002/X11 and timer T10 are never used, leaving jam alarm M190 un-set). Additionally, motor overload alarm M191 is implemented with an unlatched OUT coil, causing unexpected automatic restarts when the overload contact recloses. Similarly, clearing the E-stop circuit immediately restarts conveyor motor Y10 without requiring a manual reset. Finally, stopper release solenoid Y11 lacks necessary interlocking for Auto mode, E-stop, conveyor run state, and pallet presence.
